mainTopic: Defining an אשרה; lifting the שיתוף barrel; whether עירובין require זיכוי; a wife making an עירוב without her husband
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing the definition of an אשרה, a tree used for idol worship. It then brings שמואל's definition, and the elders of פומבדיתא rule like שמואל. Next the גמרא defends רב יהודה's rule that the שיתוף barrel must be lifted a טפח: a ברייתא's word 'משהו' is read as meaning a טפח. רב and שמואל then argue about whether the food of an עירוב must be formally given over (זיכוי), and each takes the opposite side for שיתופי מבואות and for עירובי תחומין. The story of רבי אושעיא's daughter-in-law shows that רב's view has a source among the תנאים, since רבי חייא invalidated an עירוב made without זיכוי. רב נחמן rules that every type of עירוב needs זיכוי, and he asks about עירובי תבשילין, which leads to a debate between רב יוסף and אביי. Two stories teach that a wife may make an עירוב without her husband's knowledge. The גמרא reconciles this with a ברייתא that says the opposite: it applies only where the husband would otherwise forbid his neighbors. The עמוד ends with a suggested support for שמואל, that residents may force a neighbor to build a לחי and קורה.

steps.title: End of the previous definition of an אשרה tree
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the last words of the earlier definition of an אשרה: a tree whose fruit is not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and they do not taste from its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a definition that started on the previous amud. A tree counts as an אשרה when the idolatrous priests guard it and do not eat its fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refusing to eat the fruit shows that the tree is set aside for idol worship and is not an ordinary orchard tree. This first view looks at how people behave toward the tree. The next step gives a different test.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped or used for idol worship

phrases.english: and they do not taste from its fruit.
phrases.notes: End of a statement that began on the previous amud (the first view of what makes a tree an אשרה).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין טוֹעֲמִין מִפֵּירוֹתֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a definition that started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree whose fruit the idolatrous priests refuse to eat is an אשרה.

steps.title: שמואל's definition: the fruit is set aside for an idolatrous festival
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says a tree is an אשרה when people say its dates are set aside to make beer for the idol temple's festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: for example, when they say, 'These dates are for the beer of the temple of Nitzrefei, which they drink on their festival day.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different example of what makes a tree an אשרה. In his case, the fruit is used for the idol's festival instead of being left uneaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first view, the sign is that nobody eats the fruit. שמואל says the tree counts even if the fruit is eaten, as long as it is set aside for an idolatrous purpose, like beer for a pagan festival. The key factor is that the fruit is dedicated to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The temple of Nitzrefei (a pagan shrine)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
For example, when they say:
'These dates are for the beer
of the temple of Nitzrefei,
which they drink on their festival day.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different definition from the one completed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree whose fruit is set aside for an idolatrous festival is an אשרה, even if the fruit is eaten.

steps.title: The הלכה follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אמימר reports that the elders of פומבדיתא told him the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: the elders of פומבדיתא told me that the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the disagreement over how to define an אשרה. It rules like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two definitions of an אשרה, and this report decides between them. In practice, a tree counts as an אשרה when its fruit is set aside for idol worship, as שמואל said.
steps.whatToRemember: An אשרה is a tree dedicated to idol worship. The practical הלכה follows שמואל: if its fruit is set aside for an idolatrous festival, the tree is an אשרה.

phrases.english: (Ameimar said:)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets, so the line may not be said in אמימר's name.

phrases.english: And the elders of Pumbedita told me:
The halacha is in accordance with Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two definitions in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל's definition of an אשרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the barrel only needs to be lifted slightly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's rule that the שיתוף barrel must be lifted a טפח, using a ברייתא that says to lift it only 'משהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: How do you make a שיתוף for an alleyway? You bring a barrel of wine, oil, dates, dried figs, or any other kind of produce. If the barrel is his own, he has to give the others a share in it through another person. If it belongs to them, he has to let them know. And it is lifted off the ground a tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יהודה's rule earlier, that the barrel for a שיתוף must be lifted a טפח. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to say even a tiny lift is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains how to make a שיתוף: which foods can be used, giving the others a share if the barrel is his, and telling them if it is theirs. It ends by saying the barrel is lifted 'משהו', which sounds like any small amount. That seems to contradict the requirement of a full טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a שיתוף, a shared food that joins the residents of an alleyway
To give the others ownership, through someone who acquires it for them

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is only about the last word, 'משהו'. The rest of the ברייתא (what foods to use, giving a share, informing) is background and is not in dispute.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
How does one merge an alleyway?

phrases.aramaic: מְבִיאִים חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן וְשֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: One brings a barrel of wine, or of oil,
or of dates, or of dried figs,
or of other kinds of produce.
If it is his own, he must give them a share in it.
And if it is theirs, he must inform them.
And he lifts it from the ground a tiny amount!
phrases.notes: This is the whole point of the question: lifting it just a tiny bit, not the full טפח that was required.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אשרה topic and returns to רב יהודה's rule (stated earlier) about lifting the שיתוף barrel a טפח.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that the שיתוף barrel must be lifted a טפח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the barrel only needs to be lifted 'משהו', a tiny amount, which seems to mean less than a טפח is enough.

steps.title: In this ברייתא, 'משהו' means a טפח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'משהו' in this ברייתא actually means a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this 'משהו' mean here as well? A טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא's word 'משהו' as a full טפח. That removes the contradiction with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'משהו' is not taken here in its usual sense of the smallest possible amount. In this context it means a טפח. So the ברייתא agrees with רב יהודה, and his rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The barrel used for a שיתוף מבואות must be lifted a טפח. The ברייתא's 'משהו' is read as meaning a טפח.

phrases.english: What is the 'tiny amount' that it mentions here too?
A handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשֶּׁהוּ נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by explaining the meaning of the word 'משהו'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'משהו' means any tiny amount, so less than a טפח would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'משהו' here means a טפח, so the ברייתא agrees with רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about handing over the food, in two areas
steps.stepSummary: For שיתופי מבואות, רב says no זיכוי is needed and שמואל says it is. For עירובי תחומין, רב says זיכוי is needed and שמואל says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about joining the alleyways (שיתופי מבואות), רב said you do not need to give the food over to the residents, and שמואל said you do. About joining the שבת boundaries (עירובי תחומין), רב said you do need to give the food over, and שמואל said you do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an argument between רב and שמואל about whether the food has to be formally given over (לזכות) to the people it is meant for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate arguments here, and each אמורא flips sides between them. In שיתופי מבואות, רב is lenient and שמואל is strict. In עירובי תחומין, רב is strict and שמואל is lenient. This flip is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Joining the courtyards of an alleyway with shared food, so people may carry in the alley on שבת.
To formally transfer ownership of the food to others, usually through another person who acquires it for them.
Placing food at a spot so that it counts as your שבת home. This extends how far you may walk on שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. רב and שמואל switch positions. רב is lenient for שיתופי מבואות but strict for עירובי תחומין. שמואל is the reverse.

phrases.english: It was stated: regarding merging of alleyways,
Rav said: one does not need to confer possession,
phrases.notes: There is no need to transfer the food to all the residents.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: one needs to confer possession.
Regarding joining of Shabbat boundaries,
Rav said: one needs to confer possession,
and Shmuel said: one does not need to confer possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שִׁיתּוּפֵי מְבוֹאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the previous discussion about lifting the שיתוף barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שיתופי מבואות: רב says no זיכוי is needed, שמואל says it is needed. עירובי תחומין: רב says זיכוי is needed, שמואל says it is not.

steps.title: שמואל's view fits the משנה, but what is רב's reason?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows the משנה, which requires זיכוי for שיתופי מבואות and says nothing about it for עירובי תחומין. רב's reversed view needs an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to שמואל: here (for the alleyway) the משנה taught that we transfer the food, and there (for the boundaries) the משנה did not teach it. But according to רב, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's position matches the משנה. It then challenges רב, whose view seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that for a שיתוף one must transfer the food to the residents (מזכה להן). No such requirement is stated for עירובי תחומין. שמואל simply follows that wording. רב says the opposite in both cases, so the גמרא asks what his basis could be.

keyTerms.meaning: "It makes sense" or "granted." It opens the pattern: one view is fine, but the other is hard.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Shmuel —
here we learned it, and here we did not learn it.
phrases.notes: The משנה requires זיכוי for שיתופי מבואות but does not mention it for עירובי תחומין.

phrases.english: But according to Rav, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both opinions from step 6 against the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires זיכוי only for שיתופי מבואות, which is the reverse of what רב says. So רב seems to have no source.

steps.title: רב's view is a dispute among תנאים: the story begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this question is a dispute among תנאים. It starts a story that רב told: רבי אושעיא's daughter-in-law was caught outside the boundary, and her mother-in-law made an עירוב for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among תנאים. For רב יהודה said in the name of רב: There was a story with the daughter-in-law of רבי אושעיא. She went to the bathhouse, it got dark, and her mother-in-law made an עירוב (תחומין) for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב is not inventing a new idea. He is following one side of an older dispute among תנאים. It begins telling the story that proves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bathhouse was beyond the שבת boundary, so she could not walk home once שבת began. Her mother-in-law placed an עירוב for her. The question is whether that עירוב works for her even though the food was never formally transferred to her. The story continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is a dispute among תנאים." The אמורא is following one side of an older argument.

steps.confusionAlert: רב is only the one telling the story. The dispute itself is between רבי חייא and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי (quoting his father, רבי יוסי), as the next step shows.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
There was an incident with the daughter-in-law of Rabbi Oshaya
who went to the bathhouse,
phrases.notes: The bathhouse was outside the Shabbat boundary.

phrases.english: and it grew dark on her,
and her mother-in-law established an eiruv for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that רב follows one side of a dispute among תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to have no source against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows a תנא's view, which the story will show.

steps.title: רבי חייא forbids, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי objects
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא ruled the עירוב invalid. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי protested, quoting his father: whenever you can be lenient in עירובין, be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רבי חייא, and he forbade it. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said to him: "Babylonian, are you this strict in עירובין?! This is what my father said: whenever you are able to be lenient in עירובין, be lenient."
steps.whatsHappening: The story finishes. It shows two opposite views among תנאים about this kind of עירוב: רבי חייא is strict, and רבי יוסי (through his son) is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא invalidated the עירוב the mother-in-law made. If the reason was that the food was never transferred to her (the next steps show that it was), this fits the strict view that requires זיכוי for an עירובי תחומין. רבי ישמעאל quotes his father's general rule of leniency in עירובין. These two sides together are the 'dispute among תנאים' that רב relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he forbade." Here it means he declared the עירוב invalid.

steps.whatToRemember: רב's strict view on עירובי תחומין has a source in רבי חייא's strict ruling. The opposing view is רבי יוסי's principle: 'whenever you can be lenient in עירובין, be lenient.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'כל שיש לך להקל בעירובין הקל' is a famous general principle for deciding questions in הלכות עירובין.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא — וְאָסַר.
phrases.english: And the incident came before Rabbi Ḥiyya — and he prohibited.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בַּבְלַאי, כׇּל כָּךְ אַתָּה מַחְמִיר בְּעֵירוּבִין?!
phrases.english: Babylonian, are you so stringent with regard to eiruvin?!
This is what Father said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְךָ לְהָקֵל בְּעֵירוּבִין — הָקֵל.
phrases.english: Wherever you are able to be lenient with eiruvin — be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 8 and shows the two sides of the dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a dispute among תנאים which רב can rely on.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רבי אושעיא's daughter-in-law: רבי חייא was strict, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting רבי יוסי, was lenient.

steps.title: Why was the daughter-in-law's עירוב invalid?
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא is raised. Did the mother-in-law use her own food without giving ownership, or did she use the daughter-in-law's food without her knowledge?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages asked: Did the mother-in-law make the עירוב from her own food, and it failed because she never gave the daughter-in-law ownership of it? Or did she make it from the daughter-in-law's own food, and it failed because the daughter-in-law did not know about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly was wrong with the עירוב in the story, which רבי חייא ruled invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible problems. One is that the food was not the daughter-in-law's, and no זיכוי was done. The other is that the food was hers, but the עירוב was made without her consent. Only the first reading shows that זיכוי is needed for עירובי תחומין, which is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open dilemma)

steps.confusionAlert: Both options agree that the עירוב was invalid. The question is only WHY it was invalid. The answer decides whether the story can be used as a proof about זיכוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this question decides whether the story actually supports רב's view that עירובי תחומין needs זיכוי.

phrases.english: And a dilemma was raised before them:
Did she make the eruv for her from the mother-in-law's own food,
and it was invalid because she did not grant her ownership of it?
Or perhaps she made the eruv for her from the daughter-in-law's own food,
and it was invalid because it was done without her knowledge?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the exact facts of the story told in steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose food was used for the עירוב, and therefore what made it invalid: no זיכוי, or no consent?

steps.title: רבי יעקב reports from רבי יוחנן: it was the mother-in-law's food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says רבי יוחנן personally explained to him that the food was the mother-in-law's, and the problem was the missing זיכוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages, whose name was רבי יעקב, told them: רבי יוחנן explained it to me personally. She made the עירוב from the mother-in-law's food, and it was invalid because she did not grant the daughter-in-law ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: A Sage answers the question with a tradition he heard directly from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer picks the first option. The failure was the lack of זיכוי. This would mean that רבי חייא holds עירובי תחומין needs זיכוי, just like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the Sages
It was explained to me personally

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to them,
and his name was Rabbi Yaakov:
To me it was explained
by Rabbi Yochanan:
She made the eruv from the mother-in-law's food,
and it was invalid because she did not grant her ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן הַהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן, וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוחנן, the mother-in-law used her own food, and the עירוב failed because there was no זיכוי.

steps.title: רבי זירא tells רבי יעקב to check with רב יעקב בר אידי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא instructs רבי יעקב to make a detour to the Ladder of Tyre and ask the same question of רב יעקב בר אידי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי יעקב, (son of) the daughter of יעקב: When you get there, take a roundabout route, go to the Ladder of Tyre, and ask this question of רב יעקב בר אידי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי זירא sends רבי יעקב to ask a second authority, which prepares the next step where the question is actually asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after רבי יעקב's report, רבי זירא wants another source on the question. He goes as far as telling רבי יעקב to change his travel route to get it.

keyTerms.meaning: When you arrive there (in ארץ ישראל)
Take a roundabout route and go
The Ladder of Tyre (a place on the coast)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said
to Rabbi Yaakov, (son of) the daughter of Yaakov:
When you arrive there,
take a roundabout route and go to the Ladder of Tyre,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַעְיָא מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי.
phrases.english: and ask it of Rav Yaakov bar Idi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seeks a second source for the question answered in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Instruction to bring the question to רב יעקב בר אידי.

steps.title: The question is put to רב יעקב בר אידי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב asks רב יעקב בר אידי the same question: was it the mother-in-law's food with no זיכוי, or the daughter-in-law's food without her knowledge?
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: Did she make the עירוב from the mother-in-law's food, and it failed because she did not grant ownership? Or perhaps she made it from the daughter-in-law's own food, and it failed because it was done without her knowledge?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב follows רבי זירא's instruction and asks רב יעקב בר אידי the question, word for word. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the question in full because it is now being asked of a new authority. It is checking the same issue again. The facts of the story have to be clear before it can serve as proof for רב.

phrases.english: He asked him:
Did she make the eruv from the mother-in-law's food,
and it was invalid because she did not grant her ownership?
Or perhaps she made the eruv from the daughter-in-law's own food,
and it was invalid because it was done without her knowledge?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבי זירא's instruction from step 12 by repeating the question of step 10 to a new authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Confirmation from רב יעקב בר אידי of why the עירוב was invalid.

steps.title: רב יעקב בר אידי gives the same answer: her own food, but no transfer of ownership
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אידי answers that the mother-in-law used her own food, and the עירוב failed because she did not give the daughter-in-law ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She made the עירוב for her from the mother-in-law's own food, and it was invalid because she did not give her ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יעקב בר אידי answers the question from the previous step. His answer matches what רבי יוחנן said: the food belonged to the mother-in-law, and the problem was the missing זיכוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two separate authorities agree, so the explanation of the story is firmly settled. The עירוב did not fail because someone took food without permission. It failed because an עירוב for another person needs the food to be legally theirs, through זיכוי.
steps.whatToRemember: The story's עירוב was invalid only because ownership of the food was never transferred. The food itself was the mother-in-law's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רב נחמן's general rule in the next step: an עירוב made on someone's behalf requires זיכוי.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב יעקב בר אידי is answering רבי יעקב.

phrases.english: She made the eruv for her from the mother-in-law's own food,
and it was invalid because she did not grant her ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשֶּׁל חֲמוֹתָהּ עֵירְבָה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question posed in step 13 and confirms the answer from step 11. This completes the answer to step 7: רבי חייא required זיכוי for עירובי תחומין, so רב follows a תנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The food was the mother-in-law's, and the עירוב failed because there was no זיכוי.

steps.title: רב נחמן: all three kinds of עירוב require granting ownership
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן states a tradition: עירובי תחומין, עירובי חצירות and שיתופי מבואות all require זיכוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We hold that joining of boundaries, joining of courtyards and merging of alleyways all require granting ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן states a general rule. Every type of עירוב made for other people needs the food to be given to them through זיכוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן takes the strict side of both opinions from step 6. He follows רב's stringency for עירובי תחומין and שמואל's stringency for שיתופי מבואות, and adds עירובי חצירות. The word נקטינן tells us this is a received tradition, not just his own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Joining of Shabbat boundaries (extends how far one may walk)
Joining of courtyards (allows carrying between houses and courtyard)
Merging of alleyways (allows carrying in a shared alley)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the base for the question that follows: does the fourth type, עירובי תבשילין, belong on this list?

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: We hold (by tradition),
whether a joining of boundaries,
or a joining of courtyards,
or a merging of alleyways,
it is necessary to grant ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: נָקְטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the רב–שמואל dispute from step 6 by adopting the stringency of each, so that every type of עירוב requires זיכוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three types of עירוב (תחומין, חצירות, שיתופי מבואות) require זיכוי.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks: does an עירובי תבשילין require granting ownership?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן is unsure whether עירובי תבשילין also requires זיכוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן asked: Does an עירובי תבשילין require granting ownership, or does it not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן raises a question about a fourth kind of עירוב, the עירובי תבשילין. He wants to know if it follows the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תבשילין is different from the other three. It does not deal with walking or carrying. It allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת. So it is not obvious that the זיכוי rule applies to it, and that is why רב נחמן is unsure.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question he could not resolve)
Joining of cooked foods, which allows cooking on יום טוב that falls on Friday for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: עירובי תבשילין has nothing to do with carrying or walking. It is about cooking on יום טוב for שבת, even though it shares the name עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman asked:
Does an eruv tavshilin require granting ownership,
or does it not require granting ownership?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule from step 15 extends to a fourth type of עירוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עירובי תבשילין requires זיכוי like the other types of עירוב.

steps.title: רב יוסף: why ask, when שמואל already ruled on this?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that שמואל has already ruled that עירובי תבשילין requires זיכוי, so there seems to be nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is his question? Did he not hear what רב נחמן בר רב אדא said in the name of שמואל, that עירובי תבשילין requires granting ownership?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the question itself. He points out that שמואל already answered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge: a known ruling already exists. If שמואל said זיכוי is required, it seems רב נחמן had no reason to wonder.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is his question? (Why is he asking?)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וּמַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: And what is his question?
Did he not hear

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: that which Rav Nachman bar Rav Adda said
that Shmuel said:
An eruv tavshilin requires granting ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וּמַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב נחמן's question in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's question about עירובי תבשילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל already ruled that זיכוי is required, so the question looks unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: obviously רב נחמן never heard שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רב נחמן clearly had not heard שמואל's ruling, otherwise he would not have asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It is obvious that he did not hear it, for if he had heard it, why would he ask?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב נחמן's question. He says the simple explanation is that רב נחמן did not know about שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the question itself as proof. Someone who knew שמואל's answer would not ask. So רב נחמן must not have known it.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, student and colleague of רב יוסף

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It is obvious that he did not hear it.
For if he had heard it,
why would he have asked?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: פְּשִׁיטָא דְּלָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by explaining why רב נחמן asked.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: the questioner did not know the earlier ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's question makes no sense given שמואל's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question makes sense because רב נחמן never heard that ruling.

steps.title: רב יוסף: maybe he heard it but disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects אביי's reasoning: רב נחמן already disagrees with שמואל about עירובי תחומין, so his question does not prove he never heard שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did שמואל not say that עירובי תחומין does not require granting ownership, and yet רב נחמן himself said that it does?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back against אביי. He shows that רב נחמן does not always follow שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed that knowing שמואל's ruling would settle the question for רב נחמן. רב יוסף points out that for עירובי תחומין, שמואל said זיכוי is not needed, yet רב נחמן ruled it is needed (step 15). So רב נחמן may know שמואל's view on עירובי תבשילין and still not consider the matter settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (introduces a rhetorical point)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן requires זיכוי for עירובי תחומין even though שמואל does not. So his question about עירובי תבשילין may come from disagreeing with שמואל, not from not knowing his ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: The "he" (איהו) who says זיכוי is required is רב נחמן, not שמואל. שמואל is the one who said it is not required for עירובי תחומין.

phrases.english: He (Rav Yosef) said to him:
Is it not so that regarding joining of boundaries
Shmuel said:
It is not necessary to grant ownership,
and he (Rav Nachman) said: It is necessary to grant ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין מִי לָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reasoning in step 18 by pointing to רב נחמן's ruling in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's assumption that the question proves רב נחמן did not know שמואל's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן already disagrees with שמואל about עירובי תחומין, so knowing שמואל's view would not necessarily settle the question for him.

steps.title: אביי defends his reasoning about רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's comparison. In the earlier cases רב and שמואל disagree, so רב נחמן could take the stricter side of each. With עירובי תבשילין, nobody disagrees with שמואל, so if רב נחמן had heard the ruling he would have had no reason to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really a comparison?! It makes sense there, because רב and שמואל disagree, and רב נחמן is teaching us to follow the stringencies of this master and the stringencies of that master. But here, if he had really heard שמואל's ruling, is there anyone at all who disagrees?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף and defends his original point that רב נחמן must not have heard שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that רב נחמן disagrees with שמואל elsewhere, so his question proves nothing. אביי answers that those earlier cases involve a real dispute between רב and שמואל, and רב נחמן simply took the strict side of both. With עירובי תבשילין, שמואל's ruling stands with no opponent, so a student who knew it would never treat the matter as an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so now?!' A phrase that rejects a comparison as not fitting
'It makes sense / granted.' Concedes one case before contrasting it with another
Following the stringencies of one master and the stringencies of the other master
'Is there anyone who disagrees?' Here it means: no one does

steps.whatToRemember: A student may rule against his teacher when other great authorities disagree with that teacher. If a ruling is undisputed and he knows it, he would not ask about it. So רב נחמן's question shows he had not heard שמואל's ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not following only רב or only שמואל in the earlier cases. He combines the stricter side of each opinion, ruling that every type of עירוב needs זיכוי.

phrases.english: Is that really so?! (How can you compare?)
It makes sense there, because Rav and Shmuel disagree,
phrases.notes: 'There' refers to עירובי תחומין and שיתופי מבואות

phrases.english: and he (Rav Nachman) is teaching us
to follow the stringencies of this master and the stringencies of that master,
but here (with עירובי תבשילין),
if it were so that he had heard it (Shmuel's ruling),
is there anyone who disagrees?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking: no one disagrees, so there'd be no reason to ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 19 and restores אביי's inference from step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's argument that disagreeing with שמואל elsewhere explains why רב נחמן asked his question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison fails. The earlier cases involve a real dispute between רב and שמואל, while שמואל's ruling on עירובי תבשילין is undisputed.

steps.title: Neighbors ask רבי זירא about renting from the official's wife
steps.stepSummary: A non-Jewish official living near רבי זירא refuses to rent out his domain to his Jewish neighbors. They ask רבי זירא whether they may rent it from his wife instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain official who lived in רבי זירא's neighborhood. The neighbors said to him: 'Rent us your domain.' He would not rent it to them. They came before רבי זירא and asked him: 'What is the law about renting it from his wife?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new practical story and sets up a question about renting a non-Jew's domain through his wife. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jews who share a courtyard with a non-Jew cannot make an עירוב unless they rent his rights to the space (שכירות רשות). The husband refused, so the question is whether his wife has the power to rent it out without him.

keyTerms.meaning: An official or superintendent (here a non-Jew)
Rent us your domain (your rights to the courtyard)
To rent from his wife ('from his household')

phrases.english: A certain official
who lived in Rabbi Zeira's neighborhood,
they said to him: Rent us your domain,
he would not rent it to them.
They came before Rabbi Zeira
and said to him: What is the law about renting from his wife?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא טוּרְזִינָא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical topic about a wife's power to act for the household in matters of עירוב
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the wife rent out her husband's domain for an עירוב when the husband himself refused?

steps.title: רבי זירא permits renting from the wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers with a teaching that ריש לקיש quoted from רבי חנינא: a man's wife may make an עירוב without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: ריש לקיש said this in the name of a great man, and who is that? רבי חנינא. 'A man's wife may make an עירוב without his knowledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the neighbors' question by quoting an earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wife can make an עירוב for the household without asking her husband, she can also rent out his domain for the עירוב. So the neighbors may rent from her even though the husband refused.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: He said to them: Reish Lakish said as follows
in the name of a great man,
and who is he? Rabbi Chanina:
A man's wife may make an eruv
without his knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A wife may make an עירוב (and so may rent out the domain) without her husband's knowledge, following רבי חנינא.

steps.title: The same question reaches several rabbis who have no answer
steps.stepSummary: A similar case happens near רב יהודה בר אושעיא. The neighbors ask him about renting from the official's wife, but he has no tradition on it. They go to רב מתנה, who also has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain official who lived in the neighborhood of רב יהודה בר אושעיא. They said to him: 'Rent us your domain.' He would not rent it to them. They came before רב יהודה בר אושעיא and asked him: 'What is the law about renting from his wife?' He did not have the answer at hand. They came before רב מתנה, and he did not have it at hand either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, parallel story and sets up the same question again. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts match the first story, but here two rabbis in a row have no ruling ready. This builds toward the final answer, which comes with a different chain of tradition: שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it in hand (he had no tradition or answer ready)

phrases.english: A certain official who lived in the neighborhood
of Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya,
they said to him: Rent us your domain,
he would not rent it to them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: They came before Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya,
and said to him: What is the law about renting from his wife?
He did not have the answer at hand.
They came before Rav Mattana,
and he did not have the answer at hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא טוּרְזִינָא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that raises the same question as step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the neighbors rent the domain from the official's wife when he himself refused?

steps.title: רב יהודה answers in the name of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers in the name of שמואל: a man's wife may make an עירוב without his knowledge. So they may rent from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רב יהודה. He said to them: שמואל said this: 'A man's wife may make an עירוב without his knowledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה finally answers the question, quoting שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule now comes from a second source. רבי חנינא, a sage of ארץ ישראל, said it in the first story. שמואל, a sage of בבל, says it here. Both lines of tradition agree that a wife may act for the household in עירוב matters, including renting the domain, even without her husband knowing.
steps.whatToRemember: Two separate traditions, רבי חנינא and שמואל, both rule that a man's wife may make an עירוב without his knowledge. In practice, neighbors may rent a non-Jew's domain from his wife even when he refuses.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling shows that a wife has the power to act for the household in עירוב matters, which has direct practical use when a non-Jewish neighbor refuses to rent out his domain.

phrases.english: They came before Rav Yehuda,
he said to them: Shmuel said as follows:

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מְעָרֶבֶת שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: A man's wife may make an eruv without his knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 23 and repeats the ruling of step 22 through a different tradition
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A wife may make an עירוב (and so may rent out the domain) without her husband's knowledge, following שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The neighbors may rent the domain from the wife, since a wife may make an עירוב without her husband's knowledge.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a wife's עירוב without her husband's knowledge is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling with a ברייתא. It says that if women make an עירוב or שיתוף without their husbands knowing, it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Women who made an עירוב or a שיתוף without their husbands' knowledge, their עירוב is not an עירוב, and their שיתוף is not a שיתוף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of what שמואל just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 24, רב יהודה quoted שמואל that a wife may make an עירוב without her husband's knowledge. This ברייתא says plainly that such an עירוב is not valid. So how can שמואל rule against it?

keyTerms.meaning: Here, עירובי חצרות: joining courtyards so people may carry between them on שבת
שיתוף מבואות: merging an alleyway so people may carry in it

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Women who made an eruv or joined in a merging
without the knowledge of their husbands,
their eruv is not a valid eruv,
and their merging is not a valid merging!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of שמואל quoted in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a wife may make an עירוב without her husband's knowledge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says such an עירוב or שיתוף is invalid, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The two sources describe different kinds of husbands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל is speaking about a husband who would forbid his neighbors from carrying. The ברייתא is speaking about a husband who would not forbid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (שמואל) is where the husband would forbid the neighbors from carrying. That (the ברייתא) is where he would not forbid them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the husband would block his neighbors from carrying unless he joins. In that case his wife may join for him, since joining helps everyone and he can even be made to join. When he would not block anyone, there is no such reason, so she cannot make it without him, and the ברייתא applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer that splits the cases)
This one... that one (pointing to two different cases)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he would prohibit,
that is where he would not prohibit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — דְּאָסַר, הָא — דְּלָא אָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like שמואל and the ברייתא disagree about every wife's עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wife's עירוב without her husband's knowledge is valid when he would forbid the neighbors. It is invalid when he would not.

steps.title: Support from another ruling of שמואל about forcing a neighbor to join
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that this answer makes sense. Otherwise שמואל would contradict himself, since he also ruled that neighbors may force someone to join their שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is reasonable. If you do not say this, שמואל contradicts שמואל. For שמואל said: If one of the residents of an alleyway usually joins the שיתוף with the other residents, and one time he did not join, the residents may go into his house and take his share of the שיתוף from him, even against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a proof for its answer by quoting another ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allows neighbors to take a share from a resident against his will, but only in certain cases. If a wife could always make an עירוב without her husband, that limit would mean nothing. Reading the cases as split, the way Step 26 did, keeps שמואל consistent with himself.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable (introduces support for an answer)
A contradiction between one ruling of שמואל and another

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if you say otherwise, there is a difficulty:
Shmuel against Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:
One of the residents of an alleyway
who is accustomed to join the merging with the residents of the alleyway,
but this time he did not join,
the residents of the alleyway may enter his house
and take his share of their merging from him
against his will.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִם כֵּן קַשְׁיָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of Step 26 with another ruling of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The split in Step 26: a wife may act for her husband only in a certain kind of case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that neighbors may take the share of a resident who usually joins, even against his will.

steps.title: Only someone who usually joins can be forced, so the answer is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads a limit into שמואל's words. A resident who usually joins can be forced, but one who does not usually join cannot. So the answer stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he usually joins, yes, they may take his share. If he does not usually join, no. Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the exact wording of שמואל and concludes that its answer is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רגיל, meaning "usually," shows that a person cannot always be made to join against his will. So שמואל himself holds that acting on someone's behalf without his consent works only in certain cases. This fits the split between שמואל's ruling and the ברייתא, and the גמרא accepts it with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes... no (marks an inference from exact wording)
Learn from it; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: A wife's עירוב made without her husband's knowledge works only when he would otherwise forbid the neighbors from carrying, which is the case where he could be forced to join. Otherwise the ברייתא rules it invalid. The proof comes from שמואל's own wording: only someone who usually joins (רגיל) can be forced.

phrases.english: If he is accustomed, yes,
if he is not accustomed, no.
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָגִיל אִין, שֶׁאֵין רָגִיל לָא. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof from Step 27 by drawing the inference and confirming it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The split between שמואל and the ברייתא is confirmed: one may act for another without his consent only where he could be forced to join anyway.

steps.title: A suggested support for שמואל from forcing a resident to build a side post and beam
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports שמואל's ruling that neighbors may force someone to join a שיתוף. The ברייתא says residents can force a neighbor to help build a לחי and קורה for the מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that a ברייתא supports him: 'We may force him to make a side post and a crossbeam for the alleyway.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove שמואל right. It is only a suggestion ('let us say'), and the גמרא is setting up a test of this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said neighbors may force a resident to join their שיתוף, even against his will. The ברייתא says residents may force a neighbor to help build a לחי and קורה, which make carrying in the מבוי allowed. If a person can be forced in that case, it seems he can also be forced to join a שיתוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say [a source] supports him. Opens a suggested proof that may later be pushed away.
We force or compel someone, even against his will
A side post at the entrance of a מבוי that helps make carrying allowed
A crossbeam over the entrance of a מבוי that helps make carrying allowed
An alleyway that several courtyards open into

steps.confusionAlert: The word לימא ('let us say') warns you that this proof is not final. Very often the גמרא goes on to show the proof does not really work. Do not treat it as a settled conclusion yet.

phrases.english: Let us say [that a ברייתא] supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means שמואל, who said neighbors may force a resident to join their שיתוף.

phrases.english: We force him to make
phrases.notes: The other residents can compel an unwilling neighbor.

phrases.english: a side post and a crossbeam for the alleyway.
phrases.notes: These structures turn the מבוי into a space where carrying on שבת is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that שמואל holds a resident who usually joins can be forced into a שיתוף, the גמרא now looks for a ברייתא that supports this ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that neighbors may force a resident to join their שיתוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: residents may force a neighbor to make a לחי and קורה for the מבוי. This suggests that for these שבת arrangements, one person's refusal is not allowed to stop the others.
